ok.de: Der Film begann vor unserer Ankunft, also das Frühere von zwei Ereignissen: had already started.
ok.en: The film began before we arrived, so it is the earlier of two events: had already started.

wrong.de: „has started“ gehört zur Gegenwart; die Geschichte spielt in der Vergangenheit.
wrong.en: “has started” belongs to the present; the story is in the past.

wrong.de: „started“ allein heißt: Der Film begann nach unserer Ankunft. Er lief schon.
wrong.en: “started” alone says the film began after we arrived. It was already running.

wrong.de: „was starting“ ist ein Verlauf bei der Ankunft, nicht das, was davor passiert war.
wrong.en: “was starting” is a process at the moment of arrival, not what had happened before.

wrong.de: Das Frühere von zwei Ereignissen in der Vergangenheit braucht had + Partizip.
wrong.en: The earlier of two past events needs had + participle.

ok.de: „for hours“ nennt die Dauer vor „was exhausted“: had been working. Die Ursache liegt vor dem Zustand.
ok.en: “For hours” gives the duration before “was exhausted”: had been working. The cause lies before the state.

wrong.de: „has worked“ gehört zur Gegenwart; sie war erschöpft, das ist Vergangenheit.
wrong.en: “has worked” belongs to the present; she was exhausted, so we are in the past.

wrong.de: „was working“ läuft gleichzeitig mit „was exhausted“; die Ursache lag davor.
wrong.en: “was working” runs at the same time as “was exhausted”; the cause came before.

wrong.de: „works“ ist Präsens; die Geschichte spielt in der Vergangenheit.
wrong.en: “works” is present tense; the story is in the past.

ok.de: Richtig: had finished zeigt, dass das Beenden zuerst kam. Nach „after“ geht auch „finished“.
ok.en: Right: had finished shows that finishing came first. After “after”, plain “finished” works too.

wrong.de: „have finished“ gehört zur Gegenwart; „went out“ liegt in der Vergangenheit.
wrong.en: “have finished” belongs to the present; “went out” is in the past.

wrong.de: Nach „after“ zeigt had + Partizip, welche Handlung zuerst kam.
wrong.en: After “after”, had + participle shows which action came first.

ok.de: „By the time I joined“ + Vergangenheit: Der Kunde war vorher gegangen, also had already left.
ok.en: “By the time I joined” + past: the client had left before that, so had already left.

wrong.de: „is leaving“ ist Gegenwart; „joined“ steht in der Vergangenheit.
wrong.en: “is leaving” is present tense; “joined” is in the past.

wrong.de: „would leave“ schaut nach vorn, nicht auf etwas, das davor lag.
wrong.en: “would leave” looks ahead, not back at something that came before.

wrong.de: „has left“ gehört zur Gegenwart; der Kunde war vor meinem Einstieg gegangen.
wrong.en: “has left” belongs to the present; the client had gone before I joined.

ok.de: „for months“ nennt die Dauer vor der Unterschrift in der Vergangenheit: had been negotiating, nicht have been.
ok.en: “For months” gives the duration before the signing in the past: had been negotiating, not have been.

wrong.de: „have been negotiating“ reicht bis jetzt; die Unterschrift liegt in der Vergangenheit.
wrong.en: “have been negotiating” runs up to now; the signing is in the past.

wrong.de: „negotiated“ nennt nur die Handlung, nicht die Dauer bis zur Unterschrift.
wrong.en: “negotiated” names only the action, not the duration up to the signing.

wrong.de: „were negotiating“ ist ein Verlauf zum Zeitpunkt, nicht die Dauer davor.
wrong.en: “were negotiating” is a process at that moment, not the duration before it.

ok.de: „It was the first time“ steht in der Vergangenheit, die Erfahrung liegt davor: had handled (im Präsens wäre has handled).
ok.en: “It was the first time” is in the past and the experience lies before it: had handled (in the present it would be has handled).

wrong.de: „would handle“ schaut nach vorn; hier geht es um etwas, das davor lag.
wrong.en: “would handle” looks ahead; here it is about something that came before.

wrong.de: „has handled“ gehört zur Gegenwart: „It is the first time …“ steht im Präsens.
wrong.en: “has handled” belongs to the present (“It is the first time …”).

wrong.de: „was handling“ beschreibt etwas Laufendes, nicht die Erfahrung davor.
wrong.en: “was handling” describes something in progress, not the experience before.

ok.de: Richtig: Nach „No sooner“ steht had vor dem Subjekt: had we started.
ok.en: Right: after “No sooner”, had goes before the subject: had we started.

wrong.de: Nach „No sooner“ fehlen had und die Umstellung: had we started.
wrong.en: After “No sooner”, both had and the inversion are missing: had we started.

wrong.de: Das had stimmt, muss aber nach „No sooner“ vor das Subjekt: had we started.
wrong.en: The had is right, but after “No sooner” it must come before the subject: had we started.

wrong.de: „did we start“ ist Past Simple; „No sooner … than“ verlangt had we started.
wrong.en: “did we start” is Past Simple; “No sooner … than” needs had we started.

ok.de: „since 5 a.m.“ bis zum Anruf um Mittag: Dauer vor einem Zeitpunkt in der Vergangenheit, had been working.
ok.en: “Since 5 a.m.” up to the noon call: duration before a point in the past, had been working.

wrong.de: „worked“ nennt nur die Handlung, nicht die Dauer seit 5 Uhr bis zum Anruf.
wrong.en: “worked” names only the action, not the duration from 5 a.m. up to the call.

wrong.de: „works“ ist Präsens; der Anruf liegt in der Vergangenheit.
wrong.en: “works” is present tense; the call lies in the past.

wrong.de: „was working since“ geht nicht: since braucht die Perfektform had been.
wrong.en: “was working since” does not work: since needs the perfect form had been.

ok.de: „the month before“ legt den Umzug vor das Gefühl: Das Frühere steht im Past Perfect, had moved.
ok.en: “The month before” places the move before the feeling: the earlier event takes the Past Perfect, had moved.

wrong.de: „would move“ schaut nach vorn; der Umzug war schon im Monat davor.
wrong.en: “would move” looks ahead; the move happened the month before.

wrong.de: „has moved“ gehört zur Gegenwart; „the month before“ liegt in der Vergangenheit.
wrong.en: “has moved” belongs to the present; “the month before” is in the past.

wrong.de: „moves“ ist Präsens; der Satz steht in der Vergangenheit („felt“).
wrong.en: “moves” is present tense; the sentence is in the past (“felt”).

ok.de: „By the time“ + Vergangenheit: Ich hatte das Problem schon vor dem Rückruf behoben: had fixed.
ok.en: “By the time” + past: I had already fixed the problem before the callback: had fixed.

wrong.de: „has fixed“ gehört zur Gegenwart; der Rückruf liegt in der Vergangenheit.
wrong.en: “has fixed” belongs to the present; the callback lies in the past.

wrong.de: „have fixed“ gehört zur Gegenwart; der Rückruf liegt in der Vergangenheit.
wrong.en: “have fixed” belongs to the present; the callback lies in the past.

wrong.de: „fixed“ allein ordnet die Reihenfolge nicht: Das Beheben war vor dem Rückruf fertig.
wrong.en: “fixed” alone does not show the order: the fixing was done before the callback.

wrong.de: Das Frühere nach „by the time“ + Vergangenheit braucht had + Partizip.
wrong.en: The earlier event after “by the time” + past needs had + participle.

ok.de: „for an hour“ nennt die Dauer vor der Ankunft: had been discussing (had discussed geht auch, betont das Ergebnis).
ok.en: “For an hour” gives the duration before the arrival: had been discussing (had discussed also works but stresses the result).

wrong.de: „have been discussing“ reicht bis jetzt; die Ankunft liegt in der Vergangenheit.
wrong.en: “have been discussing” runs up to now; the arrival lies in the past.

wrong.de: „was discussing“ nennt nur den Verlauf bei der Ankunft, nicht die Dauer davor.
wrong.en: “was discussing” gives only the process at the arrival, not the duration before it.

wrong.de: „discussed“ allein: Die Besprechung lief schon eine Stunde vor der Ankunft.
wrong.en: “discussed” alone: the discussion had been going on for an hour before the arrival.

wrong.de: Dauer vor einem Zeitpunkt in der Vergangenheit braucht had been + -ing.
wrong.en: Duration before a past moment needs had been + -ing.

ok.de: Richtig: Nach „it was the first time“ steht had + Partizip: had closed.
ok.en: Right: after “it was the first time” comes had + participle: had closed.

wrong.de: „has closed“ gehört zur Gegenwart; „it was“ steht in der Vergangenheit.
wrong.en: “has closed” belongs to the present; “it was” is in the past.

wrong.de: „was closing“ ist ein Verlauf; hier geht es um die Erfahrung davor.
wrong.en: “was closing” is a process; here it is about the experience before.

wrong.de: „closed“ allein: Die Erfahrung liegt eine Stufe vor „was“ → had closed.
wrong.en: “closed” alone: the experience sits one step before “was” → had closed.

wrong.de: Nach „the first time“ in der Vergangenheit steht had + Partizip.
wrong.en: After “the first time” in a past story comes had + participle.

ok.de: „already“ zeigt: Das Kochen war vor meiner Heimkehr fertig. Das Frühere braucht had cooked.
ok.en: “Already” shows the cooking was done before I got home. The earlier event needs had cooked.

wrong.de: „has cooked“ gehört zur Gegenwart; „got home“ liegt in der Vergangenheit.
wrong.en: “has cooked” belongs to the present; “got home” is in the past.

wrong.de: „was cooking“ wäre ein Verlauf; „already“ zeigt: Es war schon fertig.
wrong.en: “was cooking” would be a process; “already” shows it was done.

wrong.de: „cooked“ allein ordnet die Reihenfolge nicht; das Kochen war schon vorbei.
wrong.en: “cooked” alone does not show the order; the cooking was already over.

wrong.de: Das Frühere von zwei Ereignissen in der Vergangenheit braucht had + Partizip.
wrong.en: The earlier of two past events needs had + participle.

ok.de: „By the time“ + Vergangenheit: Sie waren schon weg, bevor das Update fertig war, also had gone.
ok.en: “By the time” + past: they had already left before the update finished, so had gone.

wrong.de: „have gone“ gehört zur Gegenwart; das Update liegt in der Vergangenheit.
wrong.en: “have gone” belongs to the present; the update lies in the past.

wrong.de: „went“ allein ordnet die Reihenfolge nicht; sie waren schon vorher gegangen.
wrong.en: “went” alone does not show the order; they had gone earlier.

wrong.de: „gone“ braucht ein Hilfsverb: had gone.
wrong.en: “gone” needs an auxiliary: had gone.

wrong.de: Das Frühere nach „by the time“ + Vergangenheit braucht had + Partizip.
wrong.en: The earlier event after “by the time” + past needs had + participle.

ok.de: Montag lag vor dem Anruf am Dienstag: Das Frühere der beiden Ereignisse steht im Past Perfect, had already sent.
ok.en: Monday came before Tuesday's call: the earlier of the two events takes the Past Perfect, had already sent.

wrong.de: „have sent“ gehört zur Gegenwart; der Anruf liegt in der Vergangenheit.
wrong.en: “have sent” belongs to the present; the call lies in the past.

wrong.de: „has sent“ gehört zur Gegenwart; der Anruf liegt in der Vergangenheit.
wrong.en: “has sent” belongs to the present; the call lies in the past.

wrong.de: „sent“ allein ordnet die Reihenfolge nicht: Montag lag vor dem Anruf am Dienstag.
wrong.en: “sent” alone does not show the order: Monday came before the call on Tuesday.

wrong.de: Das Frühere von zwei Ereignissen in der Vergangenheit braucht had + Partizip.
wrong.en: The earlier of two past events needs had + participle.

ok.de: „for two hours“ nennt die Dauer bis zum Anruf (Vergangenheit): had been working, nicht was working.
ok.en: “For two hours” gives the duration up to the call (past): had been working, not was working.

wrong.de: „was working“ passt nicht zu „for two hours“: Die Dauer braucht had been working.
wrong.en: “was working” does not fit “for two hours”: the duration needs had been working.

wrong.de: „has/have been working“ reicht bis jetzt; der Anruf liegt in der Vergangenheit.
wrong.en: “has/have been working” runs up to now; the call lies in the past.

wrong.de: „worked“ allein nennt nicht die Dauer bis zum Anruf; sie arbeitete noch.
wrong.en: “worked” alone does not give the duration up to the call; she was still working.

wrong.de: Dauer vor einem Zeitpunkt in der Vergangenheit braucht had been + -ing.
wrong.en: Duration before a past moment needs had been + -ing.

ok.de: Sie hatten schon begonnen, bevor ich ankam. Das Frühere braucht had started, nicht started.
ok.en: They had already begun before I arrived. The earlier event needs had started, not started.

wrong.de: „has started“ gehört zur Gegenwart; „arrived“ steht in der Vergangenheit.
wrong.en: “has started” belongs to the present; “arrived” is in the past.

wrong.de: „have started“ gehört zur Gegenwart; „arrived“ steht in der Vergangenheit.
wrong.en: “have started” belongs to the present; “arrived” is in the past.

wrong.de: „started“ allein heißt: Sie begannen nach meiner Ankunft. Es lief schon.
wrong.en: “started” alone says they began after I arrived. It was already under way.

wrong.de: Das Frühere von zwei Ereignissen in der Vergangenheit braucht had + Partizip.
wrong.en: The earlier of two past events needs had + participle.

ok.de: Nach „told“ (Vergangenheit) rutscht will zu would zurück: he would call. „the next day“ bestätigt die indirekte Rede.
ok.en: After “told” (past) will shifts back to would: he would call. “The next day” confirms reported speech.

wrong.de: „will“ bleibt nicht stehen: Nach „told“ wird daraus would.
wrong.en: “will” does not stay: after “told” it becomes would.

wrong.de: „calls“ ist Präsens; „told“ steht in der Vergangenheit, das Berichtete rutscht zurück.
wrong.en: “calls” is present tense; “told” is past, so the reported part moves back.

wrong.de: Nach einem Verb der Vergangenheit rutscht die Zeit zurück: will → would.
wrong.en: After a past reporting verb the tense moves back: will → would.

ok.de: In der Vergangenheit heißt das Hilfsverb had, nicht have: the film had already started.
ok.en: In the past the auxiliary is had, not have: the film had already started.

wrong.de: „has started“ gehört zur Gegenwart; „arrived“ steht in der Vergangenheit.
wrong.en: “has started” belongs to the present; “arrived” is in the past.

wrong.de: „have“ zieht den Satz in die Gegenwart und passt auch nicht zu „film“: had.
wrong.en: “have” pulls the sentence into the present and does not fit “film”: had.

wrong.de: „started“ allein: Der Film lief schon vor der Ankunft → had already started.
wrong.en: “started” alone: the film was already running before we arrived → had already started.

wrong.de: Das Frühere nach „by the time“ + Vergangenheit braucht had + Partizip.
wrong.en: The earlier event after “by the time” + past needs had + participle.
